experiment: K6: 100,000 structurally distinct, cost-aware generated strategy documents, each evaluated as ONE pooled candidate per admitted timeframe over a named universe (E-4's pooling and N_eff), screened by rung 0 run alone, then the fail-fast ladder (rungs 0 to 5, holdout deferred) on the screen's survivors, deflated at a trial count fixed now and never lowered.
status: DRAFT 2026-10-10. NOT FILED. It is filed only (a) after E-4's process P0 has been run on the Mac and read for both timeframes (research/preregistration/pooled_universe_e4.json, decision rule 2), (b) if neither F1 (size) nor F2 (calibration of N_eff) falsified E-4 on a timeframe K6 would run, and (c) on the operator's approval. Until the status reads FILED, scripts/campaign_k6.py refuses every evidence run (--data-root) and runs only the harness. A change to anything below after filing is a new campaign id, not an edit.

depends_on.e4_p0: research/reports/e4_pooled/e4_p0_H4.json and e4_p0_D1.json, merged, complete, admitted by pooled_universe_study.p0_admits; K6 runs a timeframe only where E-4's P0 admits it
depends_on.e4_main_stage: not required: K6 does not read E-4's main-stage results, and its prior trial count already includes every E-4 trial (21,968)
depends_on.why: K6 relies on pooling with N_eff being correctly sized (E-4 P0, H0_size and H_calibration). Running 100,000 pooled candidates before that is known would multiply an uncalibrated procedure by 100,000.

motivation: K1 to K5 and E-4's plan cover about 6,700 candidates and cells; none passed. E-1 and E-2 showed the binding constraint is trades per candidate (median 90 to 330 on twenty years against MinTRL_95 = 425 at a 0.08 per-trade Sharpe), not the thresholds. E-4 pools a document across 16 series with an effective-N correction to address exactly that. The operator asked for '100,000 more' strategies. This filing makes that request a single pre-registered campaign whose every document counts in the deflation, rather than 100,000 unrecorded looks.
question: Among 100,000 generated recombinations of seven documented mechanisms (state x entry event x confirmation x regime x filter x exit x direction), evaluated as pooled candidates under v2.1.0-calibrated with N_eff, does any clear rungs 0 to 5 at the declared trial count?
what_it_can_and_cannot_say: The deflation bar grows with the trial count like sqrt(2 ln N): the expected maximum of N null z-scores is 4.05 at E-4's N = 21,968 and 4.73 at K6's declared N = 495,290 (sqrt(2 ln N) = 4.47 and 5.12). Going from about 22 thousand to about 495 thousand trials therefore raises the bar by about 17%, not by a factor of 20: multiple testing is cheap in N, and expensive in what it still demands. In per-trade Sharpe, with T effective (pooled, N_eff) trades, a deflated Sharpe of 0.95 needs roughly SR >= (E[max Z] + 1.645) / sqrt(T): at T = 1,000 about 0.2015, at T = 2,000 about 0.1425, at T = 4,000 about 0.1007. Certifying a 0.08 per-trade edge needs about 6,344 effective trades (it needs 5,066 already at E-4's N); a 0.12 edge about 2,820. E-4 expects N_eff of roughly 1,300 to 3,500 on H4 (16 sleeves, DEFF 1.5 to 4), so K6 can certify only per-trade Sharpes of about 0.11 to 0.18 or more on H4, and on D1 (tens of trades per sleeve, N_eff of a few hundred) nothing below about 0.3 to 0.5. K1 to K5 give no reason to expect edges that large in these families. A null result from K6 says 'no edge of about 0.11+ per trade in this grammar'; it says nothing about 0.03 to 0.08 edges, which this platform cannot certify at any N it can reach on these bars. The arithmetic here is the plain-words Gaussian approximation (V = 1/T); the ladder's own DSR uses the per-period returns, the trials' observed Sharpe variance and their moments.

code.runner: scripts/campaign_k6.py (plan, screen, ladder, merge, status; JSON-lines shards, resume)
code.engine: engine_v3_realism through EngineEvaluator, with the signal kernel (strategy/kernel.py) and the NumPy realised-vol path (risk/accounting.py), both proven identical to the reference paths (tests/unit/test_signal_kernel_parity.py, tests/unit/test_realised_vol_fast_path.py); no stored result or cache key changes

fx_pooled_k5.source: OANDA practice MID bars, latest validated version per series, as E-4 (gate_power_study.load_series)
fx_pooled_k5.account_and_costs: GBP, IG_REALISTIC, construction_v2, official calendar enforce-where-covered: as E-4

crypto_majors_v1.status: DECLARED PLACEHOLDER. Its instruments, bars and calendar are added on wave/crypto and are not defined on this branch; the runner refuses the name until they are.
before_any_crypto_compute: its instrument list, bars_from and definition_sha256 recorded here by amendment

crypto_majors_v1.resolution: scripts/campaign_k6.resolve_universe reads fiboki.research.universes.get_universe when that module exists (wave/crypto); it resolves the NAME only, and admitted() still refuses every evidence run on it
crypto_majors_v1.trials: already counted in the declared N below (N_UNIVERSES_DECLARED = 2), whether or not it is ever run

timeframes.rule: A (universe, timeframe) runs only if that universe's P0 admits it. Documents with the London/New York window declare H4 only (D1 bars have no intraday hours); every other document declares both.
timeframes.order: H4 screen, H4 ladder, then D1 screen and ladder.

generator.distinctness: Every kept document has a structure hash (numbers elided), a rules hash (structure with universe, timeframes and family fixed) and a body hash (canonical JSON without identity, prose and universe) that no earlier kept document has; its rules hash is not any of the six seeds' or K5's hundred generated documents'. Two documents differing only in a period, threshold or multiple are the same structure and the second is dropped.
generator.cost_awareness: Stops at least 2 ATR(14) (3 ATR under a time exit; a 1-ATR floor under a swing stop), R targets at least 2R, ATR targets at least 3 ATR, time exits at least 20 bars, no H1. Costs are measured per document by the screen (cost share of gross P&L), not assumed small.
generator.grid: at most three declared parameters, each a two-value choice: at most 8 grid points (K5's shape)
generator.reproduce: python research/generate_families_k6.py --check (about an hour on one core)

stages.S0a_signal_bound: Per document and timeframe: the pooled signal count over the research window at the default binding, from the signal kernel without the engine (EngineEvaluator.signal_count). Trades never exceed signals and N_eff <= N, so a pooled count below rung 0's floor (150) cannot pass rung 0; such a document is recorded as failed at S0a and its engine runs are skipped. Removes nothing rung 0 keeps.
stages.S0b_rung0: Rung 0 of the production ladder alone (SanityRung plus the rung-0 gate block: n_trades_over_min_trl on N_eff, the 150 floor, positive expectancy, no degeneracies), default binding, research window, every sleeve. A document passes the screen exactly when the fail-fast ladder would pass rung 0 (tests/unit/test_campaign_k6.py pins the equivalence). Records N, N_eff, DEFF, expectancy, MinTRL, and the cost split.
stages.S1_ladder: Screen survivors in generation-index order, at most 5,000 per (universe, timeframe): ValidationLadder.run, fail-fast, rungs 0 to 5, holdout deferred (rungs_with_deferred_holdout), external_trial_count = declared N - the candidate's own grid points. Every report written, pass or fail.
stages.cap_rule: If more than the cap survive the screen, the first cap survivors by generation index are laddered (an order fixed by the seed, not by any outcome); the rest are reported as 'survived S0, not laddered' and no verdict is drawn about them. They are already counted in N.
stages.sharding: interleaved shards (k, k+n, ...), so a partial run is a random subsample of the generation order

gates.pooled_n_eff: as E-4: N_eff = N / DEFF replaces N at rung 0, rung 2's OOS-fold floor and rung 6's floor only
gates.no_threshold_moves: Nothing in K6 changes a gate. A gate lowered until something passes would be V1 again.

trial_accounting.unit: one (document, universe, timeframe) at its default binding is one trial; a laddered survivor adds its other grid points
trial_accounting.prior: 21,968 = E-4's true N, which contains K5's 20,904
trial_accounting.formula: declared_true_n = prior + 2 universes x screen trials (both timeframes) + 2 universes x 2 timeframes x cap x 7
rules: Every one of the 100,000 documents counts, whether it fails S0a, S0b, the ladder, or is never run because a stop rule fired.

The declared N is fixed here, before any result, and is never lowered: not if a timeframe is not admitted, not if the crypto universe is never run, not if fewer survivors than the cap reach the ladder.
external_trial_count for a laddered candidate = declared_true_n - its own grid points.
Default-binding trials are counted at the screen and again inside the survivor's grid: conservative, deliberately.
Every later campaign on these bars declares at least 495,290.

deflation_arithmetic.plain_words: E[max of N null z-scores] = 4.049 at N = 21,968 and 4.727 at N = 495,290; it grows like sqrt(2 ln N). The certifiable per-trade Sharpe at DSR 0.95 is roughly (E[max Z] + 1.645) / sqrt(T) for T effective trades.

holdout_handling: K6 reads NO holdout. Every rung below 6 is asserted against every constituent's holdout (E-4's PooledHoldoutRegistry); rung 6 is deferred.

A K6 survivor is a hypothesis. It may be re-authored as a seed with its own written economic story under its own filing; that filing is where its single holdout look is spent (one look, keyed on the content hash, by the holdout command), and that filing's trial count includes K6's declared N.
No survivor, however strong, is promoted, paper-traded or quoted as performance from K6.

expectations_stated_before_results.screen: H4: the screen passes a document only when its default binding is already significant at about the 5% level on N_eff after costs (n_eff >= MinTRL_95). With no true edge and costs pushing expectancy negative, expect 1% to 5% of H4 documents to pass (1,000 to 5,000), fewer on D1. S0a removes few FX documents (16 sleeves pool hundreds of signals).
expectations_stated_before_results.ladder: Most survivors die at rung 2 (walk-forward) or rung 4 (plateau), as in K5; any that reach rung 5 die at deflation at this N.
expectations_stated_before_results.survivors: Zero survivors of rungs 0 to 5 is the expected outcome.
expectations_stated_before_results.families: No family is expected to differ from another by more than the screen's sampling noise.

falsification_and_alarms: If more than 10% of H4 documents pass the screen, the screen or the pooling is suspected before any market explanation: stop, report, and check P0's calibration against the screen's z-statistics.
If one family supplies more than half of all survivors, report it as a family-level observation, not a strategy.
Any error rate above 1% of rows after the first 1,000 documents stops the stage (an instrument bug).
decision_rule: 1. Before any evidence run: research/generate_families_k6.py --check reproduces cells_sha256 and hash_chain_sha256; campaign_k6.py plan --check reproduces the declared N.
2. Per (universe, timeframe): run only if that universe's P0 admits the timeframe.
3. Run S0 on every document of that timeframe (interleaved shards), merge (refuses gaps and overlaps).
4. Run S1 on the survivors up to the cap, merge.
5. Report every row; survivors of rungs 0 to 5 are listed as hypotheses with their family, cell code and binding constraint. No holdout is read.
6. The ledger entry states the declared N, the rows run, the rows not run (and why), and the certifiable effect size at the realised N_eff.

compute.basis: scripts/k6_engine_benchmark.py on synthetic H4 bars in the cloud sandbox (2 shared CPUs, not the Mac): before the K6 engine change 945 to 1,011 us per bar (mean 5.7 s per 6,000-bar and 15.8 s per 15,600-bar document-series); after, 160 to 190 us per bar (1.15 s and 2.49 s; 5.1 s at 31,200 bars), identical ledgers on all 16 before/after pairs (and again after the final engine commit, when a heavier concurrent load made the same runs 1.50 s and 4.11 s: timings here carry +-50% noise from the shared CPUs). E-1 process 2 measured about 8.1 s per H4 backtest per shard-core on the Mac before the change.
compute.screen_work_fx: H4: 100,000 documents x 16 sleeves = 1.6 million default-binding backtests over the research window; D1: 66,661 documents x 16 = 1,066,576 (each about a sixth of an H4 run).
compute.screen_measured_here: scripts/k6_engine_benchmark.py --k6-screen 4 --sleeves 16 --bars 26000: 25.5 s per document (30 s for one that reaches S0b, 6.5 s for one stopped at S0a), peak resident 278 MB per process; synthetic USD sleeves, this sandbox.
compute.estimate_mac_m1_4_shards: Two calibrations, both stated. (a) E-1's Mac figure (about 8.1 s per pre-change H4 backtest per core) against about 27 s for the same work here puts an M1 core about 3.3x faster than this sandbox: about 8 s per screened H4 document, H4 screen about 2.3 days on 4 shards. (b) Conservatively, 1.2 s per sleeve run (8.1 s / 6.5x) x 16: about 19 s per document, H4 screen about 5.5 days. D1 screen 0.4 to 1 day. Ladder: E-4's 0.36 h per full-depth generated H4 candidate / 6 = about 0.06 h; 1,000 to 5,000 survivors = 0.6 to 3 days per timeframe on 4 shards. Total about 4 to 12 days of continuous running. Step 0 of the runbook replaces this with the Mac's own figure before anything is filed.
budget_and_stop_rules: Budget: H4 screen 14 days wall, D1 screen 5 days, each ladder 5 days, on 4 shards.

After the first 2,000 documents of a stage, if the projected wall time exceeds 1.5x its budget, the stage stops. The run is reported as partial: documents not run are named, no verdict is drawn about them, and the declared N is NOT lowered.
Memory: a shard stops (resumably) above 1.5 GB resident; re-run with WORKERS=3.
A failed generate --check, plan --check or P0 admission stops everything.
compute.memory_and_disk: Per shard: one timeframe's 16 series of bars, plus one document's prepared frames and its in-memory evaluation cache (released per document): 278 MB peak measured here for a screen process (Linux, synthetic bars); a ladder shard holds a candidate's whole cache, estimated 0.5 to 1.5 GB as in E-4; not measured on the Mac. Disk: about 0.5 KB per screen row (about 100 MB for both timeframes), one ValidationReport per laddered survivor (a few hundred MB at the cap).

data_rules: Bars through gate_power_study.load_series exactly as E-4: latest validated version per series, K5's bars_from trim, mid bars, the GBP FX source; a series without a GBP conversion is skipped and recorded, never invented.
The research window is each constituent's [first bar, holdout start) as run_validation defines it (DEFAULT_HOLDOUT_FRACTION); no stage reads a holdout bar.
decision_date: None while DRAFT. Set at filing: the day both merged screen files for the admitted timeframes exist for the screen; the ladder's on the day its merged file exists.
